entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 By occasion of the quarrel, Sheba makes a party in Israel. 3 David's ten concubines are put in confinement for life. 4 Amasa, made captain over Judah, is slain by Joab. 14 Joab pursues Sheba unto Abel. 16 A wise woman saves the city by Sheba's head. 23 David's officers.

And there. 19:41-43; Ps 34:19 a man. 23:6; De 13:13; Jud 19:22; 1Sa 2:12; 30:22; Ps 17:13; Pr 26:21 Hab 1:12,13 he blew. 15:10; Jud 3:27; Pr 24:21,22; 25:8 We have. 19:43; 1Ki 12:16; 2Ch 10:6; Lu 19:14,27

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:3
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
ten women. 15:16; 16:21,22 and put.The confinement and retired maintenance of these women was the only measure which in justice and prudence could be adopted. In China, when an emperor dies, all his women are removed to an edifice called the palace of chastity, situated within the palace, in which they are shut up for the remainder of their lives.

ward. Heb. an house of ward. Ge 40:3 shut. Heb. bound. living in widowhood. Heb. in widowhoodof life.

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:6
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Abishai. 2:18; 3:30,39; 10:9,10,14; 18:2,12; 21:17; 23:18; 1Sa 26:6 1Ch 11:20; 18:12 do us. 19:7 thy lord's. 11:11; 1Ki 1:33 escape us. Heb. deliver himself from our eyes.

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:9
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Art thou. Ps 55:21; Pr 26:24-26; Mic 7:2 took Amasa.Thevenot says, that among the Turks it is a great afront to take one by the beard, unless it be to kiss him, in which case they often do it. D'Arvieux, describing an assembly of Arab emirs at an entertainment, says, "After the usual civilities, caresses, kissings of the beard, and of the hand, which every one gave and received according to his rank and dignity, they sat down upon mats." The doing this by the Arab emirs corresponds with the conduct of Joab, and illustrates this horrid assassination.

to kiss him. Mt 26:48,49; Lu 22:47,48

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:10
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: in Joab's. 9; Jud 3:21; 1Ch 12:2 he smote. 2:23; 3:27; Ge 4:8; 1Ki 2:5,6,31-34 and shed. Ac 1:18,19 struck him not again. Heb. doubled not his stroke. 1Sa 26:8

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Abel.Or rather, probably, Abel of Beth-Maachah, as in the next verse. It appears, from Joab having marched "through all the tribes of Israel," to have been situated in the northern confines of the land of Israel, and in the half tribe of Manasseh, east of Jordan, as that was the situation of Maachah, to which it belonged. This agrees with the situation of the Abela which Eusebius and Jerome place between Paneas, or C�sarea Philippi, and Damascus. Josephus says it was a fortified city, and a metropolis of the Israelites; and also that it belonged to the ten tribes, having been taken from the king of Damascus.

1Ki 15:20; 2Ki 15:29; 2Ch 16:4 Berites. Jos 18:25 Beeroth.

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:15
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
cast up. 2Ki 19:32; Jer 32:24; 33:4; Lu 19:43 a bank.So LXX. generally render {solelah,} by [proschoma or choma;] which latter is described by Potter as "a mount, which was raised so high as to equal, if not exceed, the top of the besieged walls. The sides were walled in with bricks or stones, or secured with strong rafters; the fore part only, being by degrees to be moved near the walls, remained bare."

it stood in the trench. or, it stood against the outmostwall. battered, etc. Heb. marred to throw down.

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:18
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: They were wont, etc. or, They plainly spake in thebeginning, saying, Surely they will ask of Abel, and so make an end. De 20:10,11

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:20
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Far be it. 23:17; Job 21:16; 22:18 that I should. 10; Pr 28:13; Jer 17:9; Lu 10:29

entries.content: a man. 1; Jud 2:9; 7:24; 2Ki 5:22; Jer 4:15; 50:19 by name. Heb. by his name. lifted. 23:18; 1Sa 24:6; 26:9 his head. 17:2,3; 2Ki 10:7; Jud 18:4-8

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:22
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: in her wisdom. Ec 7:19; 9:14-18 he blew. 1; 2:28; 18:16 retired. Heb. were scattered. And Joab. 3:28-39; 11:6-21; Ec 8:11

entries.title: 2 Samuel 20:26
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Ira. 23:38; 1Ch 11:40 Ithrite. Jairite. Jud 10:4,5 chief ruler. or, prince. 8:18; Ge 41:43,45; Ex 2:14,16 The Hebrew is {cohen ledawid,} which might be rendered, a priest of David; and so the Septuagint, Vulgate, Syriac, and Arabic. The Chaldee has {rav,} a chief or prince: probably he was a kind of domestic chaplain or seer to the king.
